For nucleophilic acyl substitution reactions, the reactivity order is typically based on the leaving group's ability to leave. The general reactivity order is:

Acid chlorides > Anhydrides > Esters > Amides > Carboxylates

This is because a better leaving group (more stable after leaving) makes the compound more reactive in nucleophilic acyl substitution.

Based on this understanding:
- Acid chloride (O=C(Cl)C1CCCCC1) is most reactive
- Anhydride (O=C1C=CC(O1)=O) is intermediate
- Carboxylate (O=C([O-])C1=CC=CC=C1) is least reactive

So, from least to most reactive:
O=C([O-])C1=CC=CC=C1 (carboxylate), O=C1C=CC(O1)=O (anhydride), O=C(Cl)C1CCCCC1 (acid chloride)
